name: Module 4: sublibrary split and index PCR
description: Step 15. Takes the pooled, hairpin-ligated capsule suspension and divides it into four sublibraries, each of which receives its own index primer and is thermocycled in place. 30 x 20 mm, every feature 0.3 mm deep or shallower, so it is hot-embossed in COC rather than printed: resin inhibits PCR and general-purpose resin softens near 73 C. THE SPLIT IS NOT DONE BY GEOMETRY. A symmetric manifold would split a dense capsule suspension very unevenly (sedimentation plus the Zweifach-Fung effect at a bifurcation, estimated CV 30-100%), so the four chambers are filled one at a time by an off-chip rotary valve in an interleaved palindromic order, which brings the expected CV to 3-8%. The chip is therefore four isolated reactors plus their fill lines, and the metering intelligence is off-chip. Each chamber vents through a narrow capillary-stop channel to one shared vent port: air escapes while filling, liquid halts at the constriction, so the four reactions stay isolated from each other through thermocycling despite sharing a vent. That is what keeps the four indices from mixing. Chamber volume assumes capsules are NOT swollen at this stage; if they are still at 140 um the packed volume per sublibrary is about 15 uL instead of 1.8 uL and four chambers will not fit in this envelope, in which case PCR moves to tubes. Geometry is ours; the chemistry is CapSeq, cited in protocols/module4_v1.json.
